body: WarioWare Gold is Intelligent Systems' Nintendo 3DS collection of over three hundred microgames. Wario stages a tournament with a large cash prize, expecting the proceedings to make him richer. The familiar cast supplies short stories and rapidly changing challenges, drawn from earlier games and new material. Each task arrives with only a moment to understand what is required. The collection makes that uncertainty its main pleasure: the player recognises a strange little situation, finds the necessary action and is immediately asked to understand another.

Some microgames require buttons, others use the touchscreen, microphone or the system's motion sensing. Their controls connect the collection to the different ways the series previously asked people to play. A brief prompt must become a useful movement before the time expires. Later rounds accelerate, reducing the pause between recognition and response. Lives allow a few mistakes, while boss challenges extend one idea into a longer task. The variety comes from changing the meaning of a small gesture, rather than teaching a complicated control scheme.

Gold gives the story sequences full voice acting and allows players to record alternative dialogue over them. Unlockable challenges alter the conditions around familiar microgames, introducing distractions or other constraints. Coins earned through play open further amusements and collectibles, supplying reasons to revisit the short routines. The game arrived late in the 3DS's life and gathered several generations of WarioWare around the capabilities of one machine. Its shifting inputs make the collection feel like a celebration of the hardware as well as the characters using it.
